summary: Umatilla NF lookout near Monument, Oregon: an L-4 cab on a pole tower, built 1933-35 (sources differ), destroyed or dismantled in 1956.

facts.design: L-4 cab on a round timber pole tower
facts.status_note: Destroyed or dismantled in 1956 per the register and the Heppner district report; firelookout.com says a later platform tower burned in 2024

staffing.status: lookouts named from 1934 to 1947; no end-of-staffing date in these sources

events.note: Register and Rex's page date the tower to 1935; firelookout.com gives 1933. See resolved_conflicts.
Harold Gentry named as lookout, per firelookout.com
Harold Stevens named as lookout, per firelookout.com
Gladwin E. Hudson, 17, a Heppner high school student employed as a forest service lookout here, was fatally hurt by a falling limb in a line squall (Oregonian report quoted by Rex's page)
Register says destroyed; the Heppner Ranger District annual report said it would be dismantled that season
firelookout.com says a later 10-foot wooden platform tower burned in 2024; no other source found

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and Rex's page give 1935; firelookout.com gives 1933. The record keeps 1935, which two of the three sources share.
The register gives 24 feet, Rex's page 16 feet, firelookout.com 20 feet. The record's 4.9 m equals 16 feet, so it matches Rex's page and is kept.

sources.title: Ant Hill
sources.publisher: Forest Lookouts (Oregon), Rex's Fire Lookout Page

notes_for_editor: Built year and height disagree across the three sources (1935 or 1933; 24, 16 or 20 feet); the story says so. The 2024 burn of a later 10-foot platform tower appears only on firelookout.com, which calls that tower's history in question; a follow-up search for the fire found nothing, so treat it as unconfirmed. No source describes what, if anything, remains on the site today, and none gives access or visit details, so those keys are omitted. A search surfaced an Idaho Ant Hill lookout (Clearwater NF, destroyed 1946) that is a different site and was excluded. Rex's page quotes the 1941 survey note that the lookout tower was a house on a 16-foot tower; that supports the record's 4.9 m. No correction proposed.
